questions.q: The O-acetyl derivative of benzohydroxamic acid is warmed with aqueous base. The final organic product is:
questions.explain: The phenyl group shifts to nitrogen to give phenyl isocyanate, which water converts through a carbamic acid into aniline and CO₂. The amine has one carbon fewer than the hydroxamic acid.

questions.q: Hofmann, Curtius and Lossen rearrangements all give an isocyanate. The group that leaves from nitrogen in the Lossen rearrangement is:
questions.explain: The oxygen of the hydroxamic acid is first acylated or sulfonylated, and a carboxylate or sulfonate leaves. Br⁻ leaves in Hofmann, N₂ in Curtius; OH⁻ is a poor leaving group and is the common trap.

questions.q: The O-acetyl hydroxamate of (S)-2-phenylpropanoic acid, (S)-CH₃CH(C₆H₅)CO–NH–OCOCH₃, undergoes Lossen rearrangement in aqueous base. The amine obtained is:
questions.explain: The migrating group never leaves the molecule, so the chiral carbon keeps its configuration; NH₂ takes the place of the highest-priority acyl group, so the label stays S. 2-Phenylpropan-1-amine would wrongly keep the carbonyl carbon.

questions.q: If the isocyanate formed in a Lossen rearrangement is generated in an alcohol R′OH instead of water, the product is:
questions.explain: An alcohol adds to R–N=C=O to give the carbamate R–NH–CO–OR′. An amine would give a substituted urea, and water gives the amine after loss of CO₂.
